nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: Why is agroecology considered adaptable to local contexts?
nodes.answer: Agroecology is based on the understanding that there is no one-size-fits-all solution, making it adaptable to varying local contexts.
nodes.paragraph: Environmental Systems Research (2025) 14:4 Agroecological practices are vital for sustainable agri - culture, balancing human needs with ecological health (Boutagayout et al. 2023 ; Wezel 2017 ; Wezel et al. 2014 ). They optimize local resources and knowledge, enhanc - ing biodiversity, soil health, and resilience (Chimi et al. 2024a ). Integrating diverse crops and livestock naturally manages pests and improves soil vitality (Boutagayout et al. 2023 ; George and Jafri 2014 ; Wezel 2017 ; Wezel et al. 2014 ). Techniques like cover cropping and reduced tillage foster healthy soils, while agroforestry and crop rotations stabilize ecosystems (Quintarelli et al. 2022 ; Rehman et al. 2022 ; Scavo et al. 2022 ; Tully and McAskill 2020 ). Agroecology adapts to local contexts, with no one- size-fits-all solution (Dumont et al. 2021 ; Gliessman et al. 2022 ; Liere et al. 2017 ; Sachet et al. 2021 ; Wezel et al. 2009 , 2014 , 2020 ). Altieri, Gliessman, and Nicholls emphasize process- based agriculture, promoting key ecological processes leading to farmers technological autonomy.

nodes.question: How do agroecological practices enhance biodiversity and soil health?
nodes.answer: They optimize local resources and knowledge, which in turn enhances biodiversity, soil health, and resilience.

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does agroecology promote soil health?
nodes.answer: Agroecology promotes soil health by incorporating various plant species, which enhance soil health, reduce pests, and improve overall resilience.
nodes.paragraph: Six key aspects are relevant to our discussion: crop diversity, soil health, agrofor - estry, water management, livestock integration, and local knowledge with participatory approaches(Martin et al. 2016 ; Peterson et al. 2020 ). Agroecology promotes diverse cropping sys - items, including intercropping, crop rotation, and polycultures(Mazzafera et al. 2021 ; Tang et al. 2024 ; Yang et al. 2024) ). By incorporating various plant species, agro - ecological practices enhance soil health, reduce pests, and improve overall resilience(Adedibu 2023 ; Altieri et al. 2015 ; Sintim et al. 2022 ; Wezel et al. 2014 , 2020 ). Tech - niques like cover cropping, reduced tillage, and organic matter incorporation contribute to soil fertility, structure, and microbial activity, supporting plant growth and effi - cient nutrient cycling(Gabasawa et al. 2024 ; Scavo et al. 2022 ; Sousa et al. 2024 ).
